scope: CVG-003 bounded account-scoped prescription collection filtering by encounter and patient

criteria.description: The prescription service requires AccountId and filters both encounter and patient collection queries by that account before projecting summaries; a missing runtime account fails closed.
criteria.limitations: The service proof uses the repository-local in-memory implementation; direct SQL and target RLS remain outside this slice.

criteria.description: The authenticated GET /prescriptions collection route derives tenant scope from the principal, forwards it to both filtered service methods and rejects empty filter values.
criteria.limitations: The route proof is local HTTP-shaped integration evidence; target authentication, network policy and deployed RLS are not certified.

criteria.description: A two-account fixture hydrates both accounts into one service instance with shared encounter and patient identifiers, while account A receives only its own prescription on both filtered paths.
criteria.limitations: The fixture proves application hydration and filtering, not a live multi-tenant target deployment or every clinical collection consumer.

criteria.description: The RED disclosure is recorded and the corrected bounded implementation passes focused tests, full API regression, typechecks, formatting/lint hygiene and official coverage above the repository threshold.
criteria.limitations: The repository-wide coverage result is not dedicated proof for every clinical route and does not replace browser, target or release verification.

criteria.description: An independent read-only reviewer inspected the final service, route and tests and returned PASS_BOUNDED without current Critical, High, Medium or Low-blocker findings.
criteria.limitations: The review is independent static bounded review and does not replace runtime, target, provider or production evidence.

criteria.description: The bounded result is reconciled without promoting the parent or global program; parity, clinical parity and enterprise readiness remain at their previously observed partial/open states.
criteria.limitations: Global gates are intentionally still open: general parity 98/100 with 4/11 verified, clinical parity 100/100 with 2/3 verified and enterprise readiness 95/100 with 42 PASS, 3 WARN and 1 FAIL.

gaps: This gate does not close every prescription route or clinical collection/query consumer.
PostgreSQL-backed HTTP proof for this specific filtered collection is not claimed; RLS, direct SQL and privileged-writer protocol remain separate.
Target behavior, providers, credentials, accessibility, operations, remote CI, backup/restore, remaining parity and release acceptance remain open.
conditions: Keep the existing Vue/PostgreSQL monolith and package boundaries.
Do not reintroduce a collection call without authenticated AccountId or broaden empty filters to an account-wide query.
Revalidate before changing hydration, tenant context, authorization, clinical persistence, direct SQL, target, providers, production or release scope.

authority.actor: Ricardo (repository owner), via the original consolidation brief
authority.scope: CVG-003 bounded prescription collection tenant isolation
authority.decision: Authorize reversible repository-local service/route/test correction and local verification of the account-scoped prescription collection boundary; exclude direct SQL, target, providers, credentials, production, deployment, external mutation and release acceptance.
authority.expires_or_revalidates: Revalidate before expanding beyond the application collection boundary.

next_action: Keep CVG-003 and the global program IN_PROGRESS/PARTIAL. Continue with the next separately authorized gap; do not promote this bounded result to clinical parity, enterprise readiness or release.
revalidation_triggers: Any new prescription collection/query path or direct repository consumer
Changes to runtime hydration, tenant context, authorization or clinical-entry persistence
Any expansion to PostgreSQL target, direct SQL, provider, credential, production, deployment or release acceptance
